items.caption: A Western Zhou bronze-script style form of 二, depicted as two separate horizontal strokes. The graph functions as a numeral sign for two.
items.alt: Two horizontal strokes, the upper one slightly curved and the lower one nearly straight, in a Western Zhou bronze-script style rendering.
items.selection_reason: This reported mid-Western Zhou example illustrates the character’s simple two-stroke numeral form; it is a modern redraw rather than an artifact photograph.

limitations.text: The image is attributed to a mid-Western Zhou 免簋 context, but it is a modern vector redraw. No dated earliest inscription or detailed sequence of graphic changes is established by the cited sources.
The Shuowen’s account of paired ones and the earth’s number is an early lexicographic explanation; the evidence does not establish that this was the graph’s original formation.
